bibliography.note: Crossref: Shaw, Stephanie L; Preul-Stimetz, Taylor N; Sass, Greg G (2026). Vulnerability to angling and survival of Smallmouth Bass in a northern Wisconsin lake. North American Journal of Fisheries Management (advance article; license date 25 June 2026; no volume or pages yet). Publisher's standard reuse terms, not open access.

claims.note: the abstract (seen only as CiteDrive's display) gives survival of about 80 % for males and 83 % for females, Pallette Lake, Wisconsin, 2015-2025; whether it is annual adult survival, and its estimator, need the full text

claims.claim: angler catch divided by abundance implied that each smallmouth in a Wisconsin lake could be caught 3-7 times a year, and adult survival was 80-83 %
claims.note: the abstract says estimated catch per fish implied that all bass could have been caught and released 'three to seven times in any given year'; it also reports that 42 % of tagged fish were never reported caught and that less than half the population appeared highly vulnerable to angling, which the paper's 'each smallmouth could be caught 3-7 times' should not obscure

notes: Semantic Scholar not tried (rate-limited by parallel readers). CiteDrive offers a 'viewer' link; it was not used, since it is a third-party viewer and not the publisher's or an author's copy. The paper already marks both uses '(abstract)'; per the brief they stay unchecked until the human fetches the article (doi:10.1093/najfmt/vqag038). The abstract also reports a mean refractory period of about 31 days between recaptures and higher capture probability for males.
